title: Default relay-roles matrix: add Codex terra rows for small, low-effort slices
lead: `slicer relay-roles init` writes the owner's current lineup as its example: Codex sol first for every implementer slice, then Codex terra rows for small, low-effort work (whole slice, sliver and split part), then the Claude rows as the fallback; Grok first for reviewer, gate and architect, with Claude opus after it. What happens when a row's agent is not installed is an open owner question below.
findings_note: Owner 2026-11-03 (ork session): update the default matrix that slicer relay-roles init writes (skeleton() in src/slicer/roles.py, rows r1-r11) to match the owner's current matrix: add Codex gpt-6.1-terra implementer rows after the sol row (r9) and before the Claude rows it falls back to: terra xhigh for a slice of size M at effort 2, then terra high for size S or M at effort 1 or 2 (a whole slice; sliver and split-part terra rows are a separate owner question). Terra is the Sonnet-class Codex model: it takes only small, low-effort slices; larger or effort-3 slices go from sol straight to the Claude rows. Open owner questions: (1) should the default also put Codex sol first for every slice and Grok first for reviewer, gate and architect with Claude opus as the fallback, as the owner's own matrices now do, or stay Claude-first because a new project may have neither vendor installed (recommend: stay Claude-first, add the terra rows as alternates after r9); (2) the sliver and split-part terra rows (medium, high) the ork matrix has. Reference: the ork project's matrix (slicer relay-roles show --root ../ork). Tests that pin the skeleton's rows change.
boundary: **Not in this slice:** changing `resolve` or `recommend` to read the environment unless the owner picks that option; changing this repo's own matrix (`.slicer/relay-roles.json`), which the owner already maintains; the relay contract text beyond one rule line.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Owner 2026-11-03 (ork session, filed from s443): update the default matrix to match the owner's current one. Owner answers recorded on this item 2026-11-03:

- Q1 yes: the default puts Codex sol first for every slice, terra rows after it, and Grok first for reviewer, gate and architect, with the Claude rows as the fallback. A new project might not have Claude either, so the default must not assume any one vendor is installed.
- Q2 yes: include the sliver and split-part terra rows (medium and high) as the ork matrix has them.
- Terra limits stay: whole-slice terra rows only for size S or M at effort 1 or 2, with terra xhigh for size M at effort 2.

What the code shows (read 2026-11-06): `roles.skeleton` (`src/slicer/roles.py:577-637`) builds eleven rows: sliver haiku (r8), whole-slice haiku and sonnet (r1-r3), split-part haiku (r4), Codex sol medium (r9, after the Claude rows), Claude opus reviewer, gate and architect (r5-r7), and two orchestrators (r10 Claude, r11 Codex); and eight rules. `resolve` (`src/slicer/roles.py:520-563`) picks the first eligible row in matrix order and "nothing here reads the environment". The relay's `role_fallback` obligation (`src/slicer/ai.py:638-645`) already moves a role whose agent process exits with an error to the next matching row. This repository's own matrix (`slicer relay-roles show`) has the whole-slice terra rows as r21 (xhigh, size M effort 2) and r19 (high, size S or M effort 1 or 2) and Grok `grok-4.7` rows r15-r17 (reviewer medium, gate medium, architect high); it has no sliver or split-part terra rows. The ork matrix, which holds those two, is outside this workspace and was not read while speccing: confirm their exact `when` and reasoning with `slicer relay-roles show --root ../ork` before writing them.

Open owner question: how the default behaves when a row's agent is not installed.

- (a) `relay-roles init` detects installed agents (for example `shutil.which` on `claude`, `codex`, `grok`) and writes only rows whose agent it finds. The file then differs by machine, and a vendor installed later needs `relay-roles add`.
- (b) `resolve` and `recommend` skip a row whose agent is not on `PATH`. The matrix stays one file for every machine, but the lineup becomes environment-dependent and `resolve`'s "reads nothing" promise and its tests change.
- (c) Write every row and read nothing; rely on the relay's `role_fallback` (an error exit moves to the next matching row) and add a rule line: "A row whose agent is not installed is skipped; the role takes its next matching row." `recommend` stays deterministic; the orchestrator skips at run time.
- (d) `relay-roles init --vendor NAME` (repeatable) writes only those vendors' rows; with no flag, every row.

Recommendation: (c), with (d) as a later option if owners ask; it keeps `init` and `recommend` deterministic and stdlib-only and reuses the fallback the contract already has.

Owner decisions, 2026-11-07: the sliver and split-part terra rows are as the ork matrix has them (read from ork's matrix on the owner's authorization): Codex gpt-6.1-terra medium and high per sliver (ork r27, r28; note 'terra X per sliver: Haiku-class Codex model'), and Codex gpt-6.1-terra medium and high per part of a split slice (ork r29, r30). Place them after the terra whole-slice rows and before the Claude sliver and split-part rows, as the spec's order test says. Whole-slice terra rows stay limited to size S or M at effort 1 or 2, with terra xhigh for size M at effort 2.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/roles.py:577-637` (`skeleton`: rows, order, notes, docstring; under (a) or (b), the detection).
- `tests/test_relay_roles.py` (the skeleton tests that pin rows: `test_Skeleton_FirstRowAndFirstRule_NumberTheExampleFromThere` `:102`, `test_Skeleton_HoldsElevenStructuredRowsAndEightRules` `:120`, `test_Skeleton_ImplementerRows_GeneralOnesAreWholeSliceAndPartRowIsSplit` `:165`, `test_Skeleton_SliverRow_BeforeGeneralImplementers` `:203`, `test_Recommend_Skeleton_ProposesTheExampleRowsForSmallAndLargeSlices` `:432`, `test_Recommend_Skeleton_SplitYesReturnsThePartRowAndSplitNoTheWholeSliceRows` `:439`, and the `Init_*` tests from `:652`).
- `docs/commands.md:68` (`relay-roles init` row: the row list), `docs/agents.md:319-324 and :335` (the example-matrix paragraph).
- `CHANGELOG.md`.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
In `tests/test_relay_roles.py`:

- `test_Skeleton_ImplementerOrder_SolThenTerraThenClaude`: the implementer rows in order are Codex sol medium (every slice), terra xhigh (size M, effort 2, whole slice), terra high (size S or M, effort 1 or 2, whole slice), the terra sliver and split-part rows, then the Claude sliver, whole-slice and split-part rows. Fails first: Claude rows lead and no terra row exists.
- `test_Skeleton_ReviewerGateArchitect_GrokFirstThenClaudeOpus`: for each of reviewer, gate and architect, the first row is Grok (`xAI`, `grok-4.7`) and the next is Claude `opus`; the architect rows match size L only. Fails first.
- `test_Recommend_Skeleton_TerraOnlyForSmallLowEffort`: with a resolve that skips sol (`select` or `prefer_agent` cannot express "skip sol", so assert on `alternatives`), an S/1 and an M/2 slice list terra among the implementer alternatives; an L/1 and an S/3 slice list no terra row. Fails first.
- `test_Skeleton_RowIdsKeepTheirMeaning`: r1-r11 keep role, `when`, agent, model and reasoning as today; the new rows take r12 on; `next_row` is past them. Fails first only if ids are renumbered; guard.
- Under (c): `test_Skeleton_Rules_NameTheMissingAgentSkip`. Under (a), (b) or (d): a test per the chosen behaviour, written after the owner answers.
- Update the existing skeleton and recommend tests above to the new rows; each is red until updated.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Get the owner's answer to the open question; read the ork matrix's sliver and split-part terra rows.
2. Tests first; confirm each fails for the reason given.
3. In `skeleton`, keep r1-r11 as they are and add new rows from r12 in this order: implementers sol (move r9 to the top of the implementer rows), terra xhigh M/2, terra high S-M/1-2, terra sliver, terra split part, then the Claude implementer rows; reviewer, gate and architect Grok rows before r5-r7; orchestrators unchanged. Notes name each row's place ("first choice", "fallback").
4. Apply the chosen missing-agent behaviour; under (c), add the rule after u8.
5. Update the docstring, `docs/commands.md:68`, `docs/agents.md:319-324 and :335` and the CHANGELOG.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `python3 -m unittest tests.test_relay_roles -v` passes.
- In a scratch project: `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m slicer relay-roles init` then `slicer relay-roles recommend` for a size S effort 1 slice names Codex sol as the implementer and Grok for reviewer and gate, and lists the terra and Claude rows as alternatives.
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests` passes; `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m slicer check` passes; `git diff --check` prints nothing.
- [HUMAN CHECK] `slicer relay-roles show` in the scratch project reads as the owner's lineup: sol, terra, Claude for implementers; Grok then Claude opus for reviewer, gate and architect.

sections.body: One commit on the slice branch: "relay-roles init: owner's lineup with Codex terra rows".
